entries.title: Finite 48-product matrix multiplication
entries.claim: The selected v2 ordinary-basis 4-by-4 construction has 48 products and 204 other operations, with plain recursive leading coefficient 59/8. The retained independent exact replay checks the finite bilinear identity and ordinary-basis straight-line program, including rejection of corrupted inputs.
assumptions: The independent replay is restricted to the exact finite ordinary-basis identity and its 204-operation program; it is not a replay of alternative-basis recurrences or a universal theorem in a prover.
The existing FP32 pilot's evaluation order and zero-ULP predicate remain its contract. Algebraic equivalence alone does not preserve floating-point output, workspace, traffic or target timing.

consumer.owner: Numerical-kernel comparison; existing inference pilot owner

entries.next_action: Choose an arithmetic domain, matrix shape ladder, finite scratch and traffic thresholds and output predicate before a candidate implementation; perform any timing comparison on CI.

entries.title: Few-type packing and scheduling
entries.claim: Jansen and Ohnesorge v4 adds constructive fixed-parameter results for vector bin packing by item types and high-multiplicity uniform/unrelated-machine makespan and load balancing by job and machine types.
assumptions: These are scoped preprint theorems, not independently replayed implementations or proofs.

A reduction must preserve actual item/job and machine types, encoding, dimensions and multiplicities. Lifetimes, precedence, fabric constraints and capability representability are not automatically included.

consumer.owner: Q5b placement and scheduling research handoff

entries.next_action: Count actual distinct item/job and machine types in a declared placement or scheduling instance, state the exact reduction and unsupported constraints, and compare with the retained finite baseline only when the reduction applies.

entries.title: Shortest-path implementation evidence scope
entries.claim: The selected practical evaluation measures particular implementations of the Duan et al. 2025 sub-sorting shortest-path algorithm. Its measured slowdowns and projected crossover do not measure the later algorithms surveyed.
assumptions: The selected experimental report was inspected, not rerun; an extrapolated crossover is not an observed improvement.
Later algorithms remain practically unmeasured here. Graph weights, representation, shapes, finite memory and legal routing constraints must match a named consumer.

consumer.owner: Named future graph-pass comparison owner; no current replacement

entries.next_action: Keep Dijkstra as the baseline. For a named graph pass, record its sizes and constraints, select a later algorithm explicitly if appropriate, and compare implementations on CI without assigning earlier measurements to it.

entries.title: Local exact two-stack lifetime placement
entries.claim: The existing host structural implementation constructs peak-load-optimal placements for its recognized bipartite-crossing interval subset. The optional planner adapter must preserve that subset's constraints and independently validate emitted candidates through the existing checker.
assumptions: The recognized adapter subset has one pool, unit alignment and single lifetime intervals; unsupported pinning, aliases, reservations and extra conflicts require refusal or retained fallback.
Endpoint reuse semantics and the existing placement checker own legality. This algorithm supplies no target admission or theorem for unrestricted static allocation.
entries.next_action: Expose the recognized subset as an optional candidate adapter, preserve the existing baseline and fallback, and check each candidate plus touching-endpoint, crossing, unsupported-constraint and malformed-input regressions.
